samples.question: This image shows one snowflake drawn in a single colour on white paper. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks near the corners are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. An arm is a long straight spoke that starts at the small hub in the middle of the snowflake and runs all the way out to the edge of the shape. The arms are evenly spaced around the hub and are separated from each other by white wedges of page. Each arm carries two short side branches near its outer end; a side branch is attached partway along an arm, does not touch the hub, and is not itself an arm. The number of arms, the length and thickness of the arms, the colour of the ink and the rotation of the whole snowflake all change from image to image. Count the arms that are actually painted in this image, and do not answer from what a snowflake normally looks like. How many arms does this snowflake have? Answer with exactly one of the integers 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9.
